passages.note: Her Yea on the conference committee report for an education omnibus covering Muncie school flexibility, third-party surveys, political-activism neutrality, school libraries and the criminal harmful-to-minors statute.

passages.provision_quote: (b) The response and appeal procedure established under subsection (a)(3) must require the governing body to review the request at the next public meeting.
passages.note: The enrolled act's new School Library chapter creates a removal-request and appeal procedure open to parents, guardians and community members, reviewed by the governing body.
The bill details page records her as Senate sponsor of HB 1447, but its digest describes only the third-party survey provisions.
passages.actor_quote: Sponsored by: Sen. Stacey Donato, Sen. Jeff Raatz.

rows.reasoning: Donato sponsored and voted Yea on HB 1447 (2023), whose new School Library chapter lets a parent, guardian or community member ask that obscene or harmful-to-minors material be removed and requires that "The response and appeal procedure established under subsection (a)(3) must require the governing body to review the request at the next public meeting." A school corporation's governing body is not "a review committee of educators and parents" finding a book unsuitable, the act does not pull a challenged book until it has been reviewed, and it does not remove any book "a parent or community member reports as inappropriate" for all students. The evidence therefore shows she favours a parent- and community-triggered removal process over leaving curation to librarians, but it does not separate the three rungs on that side.
